title: Kingdom of Arles
capsule: The Kingdom of Arles (Regnum Arelatense) emerged in 933 when Rudolf II of Upper Burgundy united his realm with the Kingdom of Provence under Hugues d'Arles, creating a composite monarchy spanning the Rhône valley, Burgundian lands, and Provence. The kingdom passed to the Holy Roman Emperor Conrad II in 1032 after the childless death of Rudolf III, and subsequent emperors claimed the Burgundian crown but exercised diminishing real authority over its lords, who gravitated toward France. The kingdom was effectively absorbed into France through a gradual process: Dauphiné was ceded to the French crown in 1349, Provence in 1481, and the formal Burgundian connection lapsed by the late fifteenth century, with 1385 reflecting the loss of the last coherent imperial jurisdictional claim.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's internal boundaries were complex and overlapping feudal jurisdictions rather than clearly demarcated lines; its outer extent is understood but internal suzerainty maps carry high uncertainty.
